record.title: Unity Insight reports lower agent navigation cost on two Unity projects
record.summary: The Unity Insight preprint describes a read-only index that links C# code with serialized Unity scenes, prefabs, ScriptableObjects and GUID references, exposing that graph to a coding agent through typed query tools. In a paired study of 28 project-specific questions across two Unity games, the authors report 53.4% fewer tokens and 51.6% lower wall time than a general-purpose exploration agent using the same model and harness; one project is internal and each question has one run per arm. The study measures navigation cost, not coding correctness or software quality, and has not been independently reproduced here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper describes Unity Insight, a persistent read-only SQLite graph joining C# code with serialized Unity assets and GUID references; an agent queries it through five typed tools for listing, globbing, search, reads and bidirectional reference traversal.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a paired study of 28 project-specific questions across two Unity games, using the same model and harness with one run per arm per question, the authors report 53.4% fewer total tokens and 51.6% less wall-clock time for the index-backed agent than for a general-purpose exploration agent. The index arm used fewer tokens on 23/28 and less time on 22/28 questions; exact paired sign tests report p=0.0009 and p=0.0037, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors state Unity Insight had shipped in production with the Tuanjie Codely agent CLI since its public launch on 28 July 2026; the inspected paper reports this deployment but the research desk did not independently verify production use.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The measured result concerns agent exploration cost on two Unity projects, one internal, and does not establish improved task correctness, software quality or coding success across external projects or other game engines.

contradictory_evidence: The study is small and vendor-authored: only 28 questions, one run per arm per question, two projects including an internal project, and no external replication. This limits generalization beyond the reported navigation-cost outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The paired 28-question evaluation was not independently replicated; one project is internal and each question has one run per arm.
The reported outcomes measure exploration cost, not downstream code correctness, successful changes or maintenance quality.
The production-shipping statement and first-public-release date were not independently verified from a contemporaneous official product record in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains reproduce, a typed index over Unity code and serialized assets could materially reduce exploration time for coding agents in asset-heavy repositories. The study reports sizable token and wall-time savings on 28 project-specific questions, but uses only two projects and one run per arm/question, so it supports a local tooling decision rather than broad agent-capability claims.
limitations: All measured results are author-reported in a preprint from the system developers; the research desk did not run the study.
The test contains 28 questions over two Unity projects, including one internal project, with one run per arm per question.
The metrics measure exploration cost and time; they do not show improved coding correctness, build success or downstream software quality.
The index is a static snapshot and has disclosed blind spots for dynamic string-based asset loading; runtime/editor state is not captured.
Production use since July is stated by the authors and was not independently confirmed from release records here.
brief.summary: The Unity Insight preprint describes a read-only index that links C# code with serialized Unity scenes, prefabs, ScriptableObjects and GUID references, exposing that graph to a coding agent through typed query tools. In a paired study of 28 project-specific questions across two Unity games, the authors report 53.4% fewer tokens and 51.6% lower wall time than a general-purpose exploration agent using the same model and harness; one project is internal and each question has one run per arm. The study measures navigation cost, not coding correctness or software quality, and has not been independently reproduced here.

technical.claimed_result: Across 28 questions on RedRunner and an internal 3D kart project, authors report 5,000,776 versus 2,332,567 total tokens (53.4% lower), 3,363 versus 1,626 wall-clock seconds (51.6% lower), and 23/28 questions with fewer tokens and 22/28 with lower wall time. Paired sign tests report p=0.0009 for tokens and p=0.0037 for wall time. One run per arm per question; same model and harness.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports session tokens and wall-clock loop time, including cache tokens and thinking tokens; it does not report monetary cost, energy, index-build cost within measured sessions, or cost per successful code change.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected preprint specifies a cross-file code–asset indexing design and reports a paired cost study. the research desk did not inspect the implementation or reproduce the metrics; the paper’s reported result concerns agent navigation cost, not end-to-end code quality.
technical.mechanism: A crawler resolves Unity GUIDs and parses code plus serialized assets into a persistent, read-only SQLite graph. The agent accesses it through typed directory listing, glob, search, read and reference-traversal tools instead of manually following GUIDs through files. The index refreshes incrementally and does not modify project files.
technical.regime: Two Unity game projects, one an open-source 2D platformer and one internal 3D kart-style project; 28 project-specific asset/script navigation questions; same agent model configuration and harness with one run per arm/question. Does not establish transfer to other engines, external repositories or coding task success.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes the experiment and reports question-level aggregate results and sign tests. the research desk did not verify a public study artifact or independently repeat the questions.
technical.strongest_baseline: A general-purpose read-only exploration agent using shell, globbing, text search, file reading and directory listing, compared with the same-model/harness index-backed agent. No code-quality or task-completion baseline is reported.

brief.title: Unity Insight reports lower agent navigation cost on two Unity projects
brief.why_it_matters: Game-engine projects distribute relevant structure across scripts, scenes, prefabs, metadata and binary assets. If these results generalize, a persistent typed index could make repository-scale agent navigation materially cheaper. Current evidence supports a promising Unity-specific design and developer-reported cost reduction on a small question set; it does not show a broader coding-quality improvement.
